outline.chapter_title: Mathematical Reasoning with LLMs: Motivation and Overview
outline.description: Introduce the challenge of mathematical reasoning for language models, the gap between closed and open models, and the DeepSeekMath project’s goals, models, and headline results.
subtopics: Why mathematical reasoning is hard for LLMs
Closed-source vs open-source performance gap
DeepSeekMath family: Base, Instruct, RL
Headline results: MATH 51.7% (no tools, no voting), 60.9% with self-consistency
GSM8K and multilingual gains
Key contributions: large-scale math corpus and GRPO
Textbook roadmap and how to read this book

outline.chapter_title: Problem Setting, Benchmarks, and Evaluation Modes
outline.description: Define the tasks, datasets, and evaluation protocols used to measure mathematical reasoning and related abilities across languages and modalities.
subtopics: Task definitions: step-by-step reasoning, tool-integrated reasoning, formal proofs
English benchmarks: GSM8K, MATH, SAT, OCW Courses, MMLU-STEM, BBH
Chinese benchmarks: MGSM-zh, CMATH, Gaokao-MathCloze, Gaokao-MathQA
Formal mathematics: miniF2F with Isabelle and Sledgehammer
Evaluation modes: tool-free CoT vs program-of-thought with Python
Self-consistency and majority voting concepts
Metrics: accuracy, Pass@K, Maj@K
Common pitfalls: contamination, answer extraction, few-shot vs zero-shot

outline.chapter_title: Engineering a Massive Math Corpus from the Web
outline.description: Detail the iterative data mining pipeline that constructs the 120B-token DeepSeekMath Corpus from Common Crawl using a fastText classifier and domain-based discovery.
subtopics: Seed corpus: OpenWebMath as positive examples
fastText classifier setup: positives and negatives, key hyperparameters
Web-scale deduplication and near-duplication
Scoring and ranking pages by classifier confidence
Token budgets explored: 40B, 80B, 120B, 160B
Domain-based mining: high-yield math domains and manual URL annotation
Four iterations to 35.5M pages and 120B tokens
Multilingual coverage with English and Chinese emphasis
Decontamination: exact 10-gram and 3-gram filtering against benchmarks
Applicability to other domains (e.g., coding)

outline.description: Empirically compare DeepSeekMath Corpus with MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2 using controlled pretraining on a 1.3B model and a consistent training recipe.
subtopics: Controlled pretraining setup on DeepSeek-LLM 1.3B
Optimizer and learning-rate schedule used in comparisons
Results across eight math benchmarks with few-shot CoT
Learning curves: higher quality at fewer tokens vs Proof-Pile-2
Effect of multilingual data on Chinese benchmarks
Scale advantages: steeper, more sustained gains at 120B tokens
Takeaways: quality, multilingual benefits, size of corpus

outline.description: Explain the continual pretraining of a 7B model initialized from a code-pretrained model, its data mixture, training settings, and comprehensive evaluations.
subtopics: Initialization from DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B
Data mixture: DeepSeekMath, AlgebraicStack, arXiv, GitHub code, general CC
Training settings: 500B tokens, batch size, context length, learning rate
CoT reasoning results on GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, MMLU-STEM, Gaokao-MathQA
Program-of-thought with Python (math, sympy) on GSM8K and MATH
Formal proof autoformalization on miniF2F using Isabelle and Sledgehammer
General reasoning and coding: MMLU, BBH, HumanEval, MBPP
Key findings: surpassing Minerva 540B; cross-lingual strengths

outline.description: Describe the construction of a 776K-example instruction-tuning dataset (English and Chinese) and the training and evaluation of the instruction-tuned model.
subtopics: SFT data formats: CoT, PoT, and tool-integrated reasoning
English sources: GSM8K, MATH (tool-integrated), MathInstruct subset, Lila-OOD
Chinese K-12 coverage across 76 sub-topics
Training recipe: concatenation to 4K, 500 steps, batch size 256, LR 5e-5
Evaluation without tools: strong step-by-step reasoning
Evaluation with tools: approaching 60% on MATH
Comparisons vs open-source 7B–70B and major closed models
Implications: data diversity and instruction formats matter

outline.chapter_title: RL Foundations for LLMs: From Rewards to PPO
outline.description: Provide the necessary reinforcement learning background, focusing on PPO’s actor–critic setup, reward modeling, KL regularization, and practical issues for LLMs.
subtopics: RL framing for LLM alignment and reasoning
PPO objective and per-token optimization
Actor–critic paradigm and value function training
Reward models and last-token reward assignment
KL penalties to a reference policy
Memory and stability challenges in PPO for LLMs
Motivation for alternative, more efficient algorithms

outline.chapter_title: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): Theory and Design
outline.description: Introduce GRPO, a PPO variant that removes the critic by using group-relative baselines, and discuss its objective, KL estimator, and memory advantages.
subtopics: Motivation: remove value function and reduce memory
Group sampling per question and relative baselines
GRPO objective and gradient clipping like PPO
Direct KL regularization with unbiased estimator
Alignment with comparative reward modeling
Efficiency and scalability considerations
Algorithmic pseudocode and training loop structure
Hyperparameters: epsilon, beta, group size

outline.chapter_title: Supervision Signals and Iterative GRPO in Practice
outline.description: Detail outcome vs process supervision under GRPO, advantage computation, iterative training of reward and policy models, and practical training settings.
subtopics: Outcome supervision: normalized end-of-output rewards
Process supervision: step-level rewards and cumulative advantages
Group normalization (mean, std) and stability
Iterative GRPO: reward model retraining with replay (10%)
Training data for RL: 144K CoT questions from GSM8K and MATH
Policy training settings: LR 1e-6, KL 0.04, max length 1024
Sampling strategy: 64 outputs per question, single update per exploration
Reward model training: initialization, LR 2e-5

outline.chapter_title: RL Outcomes: Performance Gains and Generalization
outline.description: Present the empirical effects of GRPO-based RL on DeepSeekMath-Instruct, including in-domain and out-of-domain gains and comparisons to leading models.
subtopics: In-domain improvements: GSM8K 82.9% to 88.2%, MATH 46.8% to 51.7%
Self-consistency: 64-sample 60.9% on MATH
Out-of-domain improvements: CMATH 84.6% to 88.8%
Tool-integrated reasoning performance after RL
Comparison vs open-source (7B–70B) and closed-source baselines
Ablations on supervision type and iteration benefits
Resource–performance trade-offs

outline.chapter_title: A Unified Paradigm: SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO
outline.description: Provide a unifying view of popular training methods via a common gradient factorization, and analyze data sources, reward functions, and algorithmic differences.
subtopics: Unified gradient form: data source, reward function, algorithm
Positioning SFT, RFT, DPO, Online RFT, PPO, GRPO in the framework
Data source: offline vs online sampling
Reward signals: rule-based correctness vs learned reward models
Gradient coefficients: magnitude and sign matter
Empirical findings: Online RFT > RFT over time
GRPO > Online RFT via positive/negative reinforcement
Process vs outcome supervision, iterative RL gains

outline.chapter_title: Pretraining Insights: Code Helps, arXiv Underwhelms
outline.description: Summarize lessons learned from ablations on data mixtures and training stages, highlighting code data’s benefits and the limited impact of arXiv-only corpora.
subtopics: Two-stage vs one-stage training with code and math
Code pretraining boosts tool-based and tool-free math reasoning
Mixing code and math mitigates catastrophic forgetting for coding
Math training also enhances general reasoning (MMLU, BBH)
ArXiv-only training shows minimal or negative math gains
Caveats: tasks not covered, mixtures, potential scale effects
Data quality and diversity over sheer parameter count

outline.chapter_title: Evaluation Protocols, Contamination Control, and Formal Proofing
outline.description: Codify the evaluation procedures used throughout, emphasizing decontamination rules, prompting setups, tool use, and formal proof evaluation.
subtopics: Decontamination: exact n-gram matching (10-gram primary, 3-gram fallback)
Prompting: few-shot CoT, PoT, and zero-shot settings
Program evaluation: Python execution with math/sympy
Formal evaluation: informal-to-formal with Isabelle and Sledgehammer
Metrics: accuracy, Pass@K vs Maj@K, self-consistency
Answer normalization and scoring practices
Reporting multilingual results fairly

outline.chapter_title: Limitations, Responsible Use, and Future Directions
outline.description: Discuss current limitations and risks, and outline research directions in data selection, training algorithms, and reward modeling for stronger reasoning.
subtopics: Weaker geometry and theorem-proving vs closed models
Few-shot limitations at 7B scale
Potential data-selection biases in pretraining and SFT
Advanced decoding for RL data: tree-search and better exploration
RL robustness to noisy rewards and weak-to-strong alignment
Reward model generalization, uncertainty calibration, and process rewards
Scaling data and models responsibly and reproducibly
Open problems and suggested projects for students
